label: Cautionary Tales
description: Extends a current trend toward an unwanted everyday consequence, using warning, satire, or dark design to expose hidden costs and values.

zh.label: 警示故事
zh.description: 将当下趋势延展到不愿发生的日常后果，用警示、讽刺或黑暗设计揭示被忽略的代价与价值取舍。

theory_mapping.source_notes: 思辨设计tools-3.pdf page 11, Cautionary Tales / 警示性故事.

model_constraints: Extend a real trend or value choice toward an unwanted consequence.
Keep the consequence grounded in daily life rather than apocalypse.
Show who bears the cost and which values are hidden or sacrificed.
Use negativity, satire, or dark design to create critical distance.

When a technology promises human-like autonomy, trace ordinary scaling costs such as hidden teleoperation, data labor, maintenance, liability transfer, dependence, or market narrative; do not default to apocalypse.

Test whether investment and public trust follow demonstrated task value or the story of human resemblance; make a plausible bubble or correction legible through who is left holding the maintenance, data, or care burden.
Preserve the required tool information structure while using the package output_budget; remove repeated framing and keep evidence, tables, and questions concise.

presentation.interaction_hint: Trace an everyday warning consequence before proposing a response.

recommendation.reason: Cautionary Tales are strongest when a written unwanted consequence is paired with a concrete everyday warning artifact, satirical object, or scene.
best_when: The input trend is wrapped in excessive optimism or solutionism.
The user needs to show who pays the cost of a value choice.
A public-facing warning object or dark-design scene would make the issue discussable.

avoid: fear image with no connection to a current trend

warnings: Keep the future grounded in everyday life; do not turn the output into apocalypse imagery.
